newsitem.title: USA: Investor Davis may find gaming block in Milwaukee.
newsitem.headline: Investor Davis may find gaming block in Milwaukee.

text.p: Los Angeles investor Marvin Davis is expected to have a tough time convincing Milwaukee's anti-gambling mayor to support a $75 million casino expansion project, a spokesman for Mayor John Norquist said Thursday.
"The mayor says he's willing to discuss development, but he has had a long-standing position on gambling," spokesman Jim Rowen told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"He doesn't think gambling is in the best interest of the (Menomonee) Valley or for the City of Milwaukee."

Last week, Davis signed a five-year agreement to provide up to $75 million to finance an expansion of the Potawatomi Bingo and Casino in the Menomonee Valley area, according to a spokeswoman for Davis and a press release issued by the Forest County Potawatomi Nation, owners of the casino.
The casino would be part of a project that would involve more than just adding 1,500 slot machines to the current total of 200, a casino spokesman said.
"(Davis) is exploring additional opportunities, including a possible hotel, entertainment venue and restaurants," Tom Krajewski, spokesman for the Potawatomi Bingo & Casino, said.

Krajewski said Davis Gaming would receive 25 percent of the first $100 million in revenue (after operating expenses) and 20 percent of additional net revenue. The tribe would own and manage the casino, although Davis would have approval of managerial choice, he added.
"Just to give you an idea of the scope of this, putting 1,500 machines in a casino facility alone costs between $20 million and $30 million," Krajewski said.
There is no formal expansion plan so far, he said, adding that tribe officials have stressed that their goals match those of the city in terms of job creation and job retention.

The city is considering bids for a study aimed at outlining the optimal redevelopment of the Menomonee Valley, currently home to the Milwaukeee stockyards, rail facilities and several abandoned industrial properties.
"The city has been working on a redevelopment plan for the Menomonee Valley for some time in a partnership with a business organization whose members have businesses in the Valley now," he said.
A spokesman for the Milwakee Department of City Development said final results from the study are expected sometime this fall.
"Any gambling expansion is up to (Wisconsin Governor Tommy Thompson), but the mayor is adamantly opposed to gambling expansion in the Menomonee Valley," Rowan said.
Krajewski said the governor has indicated he will "carefully consider the views of the city in making a determination."
